purpose: Close inventory-only coverage for eight identity/107 handlers and two INAV MSPv2 codecs without inventing absent functions.
summary: All six identity handlers implement only the existing identity/version rows. Both107handlers are literal no-ops. INAV MSPv2 input/output codecs are recursively instruction/constant-identical to BF counterparts, excluding debug metadata; no additional INAV-only wire feature found.

modules.reviewDepth: All original instructions and constants read; assignments and helper calls traced.
findings: Reads three U8 values through MSPP: protocol version, API major, API minor. Stores protocol version and tonumber(major.."."..minor).
No transport sends, settings writes, extra sensor fields or hidden controls.
AERODECK already retains major/minor separately; do not copy decimal API representation.

modules.reviewDepth: All original instructions and constants read; side effects enumerated.
findings: Reads fixed four-byte string via MSPP("S",4) and stores FC.FW_NAME; remaining calls are debug logging.
Actual family acceptance/rejection remains in MSPCFC, already covered. No additional capability.

modules.reviewDepth: All original instructions and constants read; family-specific stored fields traced.
findings: Reads three U8 values and formats dotted firmware version.
No extra request or control operation.

modules.reviewDepth: Entire three-instruction original handler read; zero constants/prototypes or helper calls.
findings: MSP107 handler is a literal no-op: VARARG followed by RETURN and terminal RETURN. It does not decode home distance/bearing or any field.
Catalog presence is not implementation. No 107 enqueue found in earlier scheduler/caller review.

Correction to broad earlier context wording: 107 is catalog-plus-no-op, not a functioning decoder. This strengthens the existing negative finding; it does not create another missing AERODECK capability.
modules.classification: No-op placeholder in original; not an executable parity requirement

modules.reviewDepth: Instruction/constant/control-flow inspection of codec plus recursive semantic-structure equality to already reviewed BF counterpart; no emulation or hardware execution.
findings: INAV receiver is structurally identical to BF receiver: parameters, vararg/stack, instruction words, constants, upvalue descriptors and all nested prototypes match after excluding source/debug metadata.
Traced error flag, version bits, START/sequence, little-endian command/length, command matching, continuation/reassembly, timeout/error accounting and dispatch to family C/MSPCxxxx handler.
No INAV-specific hidden command or additional data feature resides in codec. Family-specific capabilities remain in selected handlers.
Original buffers by configured chunk size and reported length; current AERODECK bounds/strict validation remain desirable and are not made equivalent by this comparison.

modules.reviewDepth: Instruction/constant/control-flow inspection of codec plus recursive semantic-structure equality to already reviewed BF counterpart; no emulation or hardware execution.
findings: INAV transmitter is structurally identical to BF transmitter under the same metadata-excluded comparison.
Traced START/version/sequence header, little-endian command/length, payload chunk packing through OUT.SIZE, pointer/sequence advancement and pushM wrapper call.
Read/write outer frame type selection remains in shared MSPWXF wrapper based on OUT.save (0x7A/0x7C), already covered. No INAV-specific control capability hidden in the codec.
This is code-structure proof, not packet execution, transport validation or hardware performance proof.

limitations: Static original bytecode review only. No keys read, activation mechanism implementation, runtime modifications, FC writes, packet execution or radio testing. Shared codec equality does not prove end-to-end INAV/FrSky support in AERODECK. Existing required missing INAV/FrSky/queue/write capabilities remain unchanged.
